summary.description: Phenol is a chemical that appears as colourless to white crystals with an antiseptic odour; technical grades may be pink crystals or liquid. It dissolves relatively well in water and occurs both naturally and as a man-made chemical.
emission_sources: Industrial waste from chemical manufacturing and resin production
environmental_impact: At normal environmental levels, phenol is unlikely to harm wildlife, plants, or humans
Long-term exposure to high concentrations (usually occupational) may cause adverse health effects
Phenols have low volatility and tend to persist in the environment

top_sdg_impacts.SDG3_Good_Health_and_Wellbeing: High concentrations of phenol can cause adverse health effects especially in occupational settings, affecting workers' wellbeing.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG12_Responsible_Consumption_and_Produc: Phenol is released as industrial waste and pesticide residues, highlighting the need for better management of chemical production and use.
top_sdg_impacts.SDG6_Clean_Water_and_Sanitation: Phenol's persistence and solubility in water mean it can contaminate water sources, impacting clean water availability and quality.
